one_liner: Small header-only rank/select bit vectors (FastBitVec, RRRBitVec) tuned on Apple Silicon; edges SDSL rank_support_v/select_support_mcl at 1M bits.
what_it_does: Provides three static bit-vector index classes in one header (include/bitvec.hpp, namespace succinct): BlockBitVec, FastBitVec and RRRBitVec, each built from a RawBits word array and exposing rank1(i), select1(j), get_total_ones() and overhead_bytes(). It is a self-contained alternative to SDSL's rank/select supports for wavelet-tree or FM-index building blocks, with its own interface rather than SDSL's (rank1 is inclusive of position i, select1 is 0-based and returns -1 when out of range).
how_it_is_fast: FastBitVec is a two-level rank directory with 4096-bit superblocks (64-bit absolute counts) and 256-bit blocks (16-bit relative counts), so a rank query is two table loads plus at most four popcounts that the compiler unrolls. Select samples every 256th set bit (uint32 positions) and then binary-searches with rank1 inside the sampled range. RRRBitVec is a Raman-Raman-Rao encoding with 15-bit blocks, 4-bit packed classes, variable-width offsets and 240-bit superblocks, decoded through precomputed class/offset/decode tables; its select narrows to one superblock via the same 1-in-256 sampling and scans at most 16 class nibbles.
when_to_use: Static bit vectors up to a few hundred million bits where rank latency matters and you want a single header with no SDSL build dependency.

Read-heavy rank workloads on ARM64 (Apple M-series) where a 1.3-1.4x gain over SDSL rank_support_v at cache-resident sizes is worth having (narrowing to about 1.26x at 100M bits per the paper's Table 1).
Select-heavy workloads at medium-to-high density where RRRBitVec's 33.7 ns select (1M bits, 50%) beats SDSL select_support_mcl's 78.4 ns in the author's runs.
Very sparse or very dense vectors where RRRBitVec's entropy coding gets below 1 bit per element (0.84 bpe at 1% density per the README).
Teaching or prototyping: about 600 lines, easy to read and adapt.
when_not_to_use: Bit vectors longer than 2^32 bits: select sample tables store positions (FastBitVec) and superblock indices (RRRBitVec) as uint32_t, so FastBitVec select breaks silently beyond about 4.29 billion bits.

When you need rank0/select0 or access on RRRBitVec: the README says all four queries are supported, but the header implements only rank1 and select1 (no rank0/select0 functions exist in bitvec.hpp or the tests).
When you need serialization, mmap loading, or dynamic updates: none are provided; every structure is rebuilt in memory from RawBits.
Sparse vectors with FastBitVec select: 256 ones span about 25,600 bits at 1% density, so select becomes a longer binary search of rank1 calls; RRRBitVec, sux/pasta or SDSL sd_vector fit better.
Space-critical uses at 50% density with RRRBitVec: its 1.695 bpe total is larger than an uncompressed vector plus FastBitVec's index (1.141 bpe).

integration.dependencies: none for the library (C++ standard library only); Google Benchmark v1.8.3 and optionally sdsl-lite for the benchmark binary
integration.min_toolchain: C++17; uses __builtin_popcountll/__builtin_popcount, so GCC or Clang (MSVC not supported as written); tested only with Apple Clang 15.0.0
integration.platforms: any 64-bit target with GCC/Clang builtins; tuned and measured only on Apple Silicon ARM64 (-march=native)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; queries are const and noexcept with no mutable state (RRR lookup tables are a function-local static, initialized thread-safely in C++11+), so concurrent reads after construction should be safe
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same role as SDSL rank_support_v/select_support_mcl but a different API (own RawBits container, inclusive rank1, -1 for missing select), no serialization, no rank0/select0

gotchas: Every index class stores a const RawBits& to the input, not a copy: the RawBits object must outlive the index, or rank/select read freed memory. RRRBitVec keeps the reference too, though it only uses the length.

rank1(i) counts ones in [0, i] inclusive, unlike SDSL's rank(i) over [0, i); the benchmark calls SDSL with i + 1 to match. FastBitVec::rank1 does no bounds check (i >= len reads past the words array); RRRBitVec::rank1 clamps to total_ones.

The SDSL space figure (1.250 bpe) counts only the rank_support_v directory, not select_support_mcl, while FastBitVec's 1.141 bpe includes its select samples; SDSL's more compact rank_support_v5 was not compared.
README clone URL (github.com/ishgarg/succinct-bitvec-cpp) points to a different account than the repo.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over SPIDER, rankselect (PTSelect) or QuadRank only when you want a tiny dependency-free header for plain rank/select on ARM64 and can live with unreviewed code; those siblings are better engineered and benchmarked against stronger baselines (pasta, poppy, rank9). For compressed bit vectors, h0_bv and LA-vector are more mature alternatives to its RRRBitVec.
verified_claims_summary: First-party Google Benchmark runs at 1M bits, 50% density, uniform random queries on an unspecified Apple Silicon M-series CPU with Apple Clang 15.0.0 and -O3 -march=native: FastBitVec rank 1.65 ns vs SDSL rank_support_v 2.25 ns, FastBitVec select 44.5 ns and RRRBitVec select 33.7 ns vs SDSL select_support_mcl 78.4 ns. The companion PDF extends rank to 100M bits, where FastBitVec's lead shrinks to about 1.26x; select is reported only at 1M bits.
status_note: Two commits on 2026-05-24, 2 stars, no issues; MIT-licensed and small enough to vendor, but it is a new single-author research companion with a README that overstates the API (rank0/select0).
